title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description:
# Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

Given an integer array `nums`, return an integer array `counts` where `counts[i]` is the number of elements to the right of `nums[i]` that are strictly smaller than `nums[i]`.

Equal values do not count as smaller. Negative values and duplicate values must be handled correctly.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [5,2,6,1]
**Output:** [2,1,1,0]
**Explanation:**
To the right of `5`, the smaller values are `2` and `1`.
To the right of `2`, the smaller value is `1`.
To the right of `6`, the smaller value is `1`.
To the right of `1`, there are no smaller values.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [-1]
**Output:** [0]

## Example 3:

**Input:** nums = [-1,-1]
**Output:** [0,0]
**Explanation:** Equal values are not strictly smaller.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4`

solutions.name: Merge Sort with Index Tracking
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store the original index of each value and run a modified merge sort. During merge, whenever a right-half value is moved before a left-half value, that right-half value is strictly smaller and sits to the right in the original split. Count how many such right-half values have already moved before each left-half index.

## Key Insight

A merge-sort split preserves the original left-to-right order between the two halves. Values in the right half are exactly elements that appear after values in the left half, so cross-half inversions give the smaller-after-self counts.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Binary Indexed Tree with Coordinate Compression
solutions.description:
## Approach

Coordinate-compress all values so negative numbers and large gaps become ranks from `1` to `u`. Scan `nums` from right to left. Before inserting the current rank, query the Fenwick tree for how many inserted ranks are smaller than it.

## Key Insight

After scanning from right to left, the data structure contains exactly the values to the right of the current index. A prefix sum up to `rank - 1` counts only strictly smaller values, so duplicates are excluded automatically.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Compressed Segment Tree Prefix Counts
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use the same coordinate compression as the Fenwick solution, but store frequencies in an iterative segment tree. For each value scanned from right to left, query the rank interval `[1, rank - 1]`, then update the current rank by one.

## Key Insight

The segment tree makes the counted interval explicit. It is the same mathematical query as the Fenwick tree, but it teaches range-query decomposition and can be extended to richer aggregate data.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Augmented Binary Search Tree
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n log n) average, O(n^2) worst case
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from right to left and insert each number into a binary search tree. Each node stores how many values are in its left subtree and how many duplicates are equal to the node value. While inserting, accumulate how many existing values are strictly smaller than the inserted value.

## Key Insight

When the inserted value goes right, every value in the current node's left subtree plus the current node's duplicates is smaller and should be added. When it goes left, the current node's `leftSize` increases, but no smaller values have been passed.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n log n) on a balanced tree shape, O(n^2) in the worst unbalanced case
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Ordered Insertion Baseline
solutions.description:
## Approach

Scan from right to left while maintaining a sorted list of values already seen. The lower-bound insertion index is exactly the number of strictly smaller values to the right. Insert the current value at that position to keep the list sorted.

## Key Insight

The sorted list is a direct model of the suffix that has already been scanned. It is slower because inserting into an array list shifts elements, but it makes the meaning of lower bound and strict comparison easy to see.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n^2)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

tests.description: single element has no right side
smaller elements may be separated by larger ones
already increasing array has no smaller suffix values
strictly decreasing array counts every suffix value
duplicates count the same smaller suffix value
negative duplicates and one lower tail value
all equal values produce zero counts
